## The blocker — a second latent defect: `_assert_sql_flags` races `printf | grep -q` under `pipefail`

`protect.sh` `_assert_sql_flags` (lines ~239–250) captures
`gcloud sql instances patch --help` (48,509 bytes here) into a variable
and tests each required flag with:

```bash
printf '%s' "$help_text" | grep -q -- "$flag"
```

The script runs `set -euo pipefail`. `grep -q` exits **on the first
match** without draining the pipe; the bash-builtin `printf` keeps
writing the remaining ~48 KB and is killed by **SIGPIPE (exit 141)**.
Under `pipefail` the pipeline's status is 141, so the `||` branch
treats a **matched** flag as missing and exits 4. It is a scheduler
race — which flags flake varies run to run; in the apply run
`--maintenance-window-day` lost it.

Offline reproduction against the same gcloud help text
(`flagcheck3-repro.sh`, six runs — `flag-grep-sigpipe-repro.txt`):

```
--deletion-protection        -> pipeline=0   PIPESTATUS=0 0     (always)
--retain-backups-on-delete   -> pipeline=141 PIPESTATUS=141 0   (flaky)
--maintenance-window-day     -> pipeline=141 PIPESTATUS=141 0   (flaky)
--maintenance-window-hour    -> pipeline=141 PIPESTATUS=141 0   (flaky)
--storage-auto-increase-limit-> pipeline=141 PIPESTATUS=141 0   (flaky)
```

`PIPESTATUS=141 0` is the tell: `grep` **matched** (its 0) while
`printf` died on EPIPE. Without `pipefail` the same pipeline is stable
(grep's 0 is the pipeline status) — which is why the defect survived:
every `printf|grep -q` site in the script except this one pipes a
tiny string that always lands before grep exits, and `gcloud --help`'s
48 KB is the only payload large enough to outlive the read end.

All five flags are genuinely advertised (verified directly on this
machine, `gcloud` 583.0.0 — lines 48–49, 444–449 of the help). The
check's refusal is a machinery defect, not a property of the
environment. The leg-runner never amends a guard mid-leg.
